sentences.text: Issi is a plateosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Triassic in Greenland.
The only known species is Issi saaneq, which translates to "cold bone".
The holotype consists of a relatively complete skull, lower jaws, and teeth.
The skull of the holotype is partly articulated.
The holotype represents a later-stage juvenile or subadult individual.
The preserved length of the holotype skull is 243.7 millimetres.
Issi is the first non-avian dinosaur species described from Greenland.
A skull of a basal sauropodomorph was uncovered on July 27, 1991, by a Harvard University team led by Farish Jenkins on Jameson Land in Greenland.
A basal sauropodomorph skull was discovered on July 27, 1991, at the Iron Cake site in northeastern Greenland.
The species Issi saaneq was named and described in 2021 by Victor Beccari Dieguez Campo, Octávio Mateus, Oliver Wings, Jesper Milàn, and Lars Bjørn Clemmensen.
In 1994, the discovery was reported in scientific literature and initially assigned to Plateosaurus engelhardti.
A smaller juvenile skull was discovered in 1995.
Three additional skeletons were excavated in 2012.
Three skeletons discovered in 2012 were not formally referred to or described in 2021.
Because the last skeleton was not fully prepared, the description was limited to the head.
In 2021, Issi was reinterpreted as a distinct genus that is the sister species of Plateosaurus.
Issi is classified within the family Plateosauridae.
The holotype and referred specimens were originally assigned to the species Plateosaurus trossingensis.
In 2021, they were reinterpreted as their own genus but remain closely related to Plateosaurus.
Issi is classified in the class Saurischia.
Issi lived approximately 214 million years ago during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic in what is now Europe.
Issi lived during the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
